To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the yellow fluorescent protein variant I152L is a highly suitable reporter of anionic fluxes into cells, and is therefore suitable for the high-throughput screening for agonists and antagonists of anionic ligand gated channels.
we have developed a high throughput screening assay for ligands acting at GABA and glycine receptor chloride channels.
a yellow fluorescent protein-based, high throughput screening assay has been developed and validated for GABA(A) and glycine Cl- channels transiently expressed in mammalian cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel ligands for the GABA(A) and glycine Cl- channels.

the design, synthesis and testing of novel ligands with a view to identifying new drugs that may prove effective for the treatment of epilepsy, anxiety and depression, or for the treatment of muscle spasms.
the development of novel fluorescent probes and the application of these probes to the study of biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the YFP-I152 and YFP-V153 are suitable for use in high throughput screening of ligands for anionic ligand gated ion channels.
the YFP-based assay is an excellent alternative to patch-clamp for high-throughput drug screening of ligand-gated ion channels.
the YFP-based assay is a highly sensitive, robust, and low-cost method for the screening of anionic ligand gated ion channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a robust, sensitive, and cost-effective assay for high-through put screening of anionic ligand gated channels.
we have developed a robust and cost-effective fluorescence assay for high-through-put screening of ligand-gated chloride channels.
we have developed an inexpensive assay for the high-throughput screening (HTS) of anionic ligand gated channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
YFP-based fluorescence assays are well suited to high-throughput screening for ligands of anionic ligand gated ion channels.
YFP variants can be used as a reporter for chloride influx in cells expressing GABA(A), glycine and GABA(C) receptors and that this can be done with a high degree of sensitivity.
the use of an anion-quenchable YFP reporter is a robust and reliable approach to the high throughput screening of ligand-gated chloride channel receptors.
